key_insight: A 16-parameter spectral eddy viscosity can be tuned online with ensemble Kalman inversion to make coarse LES spectra match DNS more closely in forced 2D turbulence.
engineering_relevance: This offers a derivative-free route to calibrate turbulence closures directly from data, improving LES fidelity without hand-tuning model constants.
method: Parameterize a wavenumber-dependent viscosity with a 16-dimensional vector.
Run an ensemble of coarse-resolution LES simulations and compare kinetic energy spectra to DNS.
Use ensemble Kalman inversion to iteratively update the closure parameters and reduce spectral mismatch.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports convergence of the spectral mismatch when LES spectra are compared against filtered DNS data up to the LES-resolved wavenumber range.
watch_item: The approach is validated in forced two-dimensional turbulence, so transferability to 3D or different flow regimes may require re-tuning and additional testing.
paper_title: Online Learning of a Spectral Eddy Viscosity Closure for Large Eddy Simulation Using Ensemble Kalman Inversion
